name: pattern-uncommitted-evidence
description: Recurring Phase 0 failure — evidence and fixtures existed on disk but were never committed; always check git ls-files, not the filesystem
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

**Always verify "committed" claims with `git ls-files` / `git status`, never with
`ls` or `find`.** A DoD item saying "committed under `fixtures/`" is not
satisfied by files merely existing in the working tree.

**Why:** in the Phase 0 audit (2026-08-19) every substantive artifact was present
on disk and genuinely correct, but untracked: `fixtures/cc-2.1.234/`,
`fixtures/PHASE0-VERDICT.md`, `fixtures/README.md`. Worse, the enabling code
change (`CLAUDE_PROJECTS_ROOT` support in `spike/tail.mjs`) was also uncommitted,
so the documented reproduction command would silently read the live `~/.claude`
instead of fixtures for anyone at HEAD. The phase looked done and was not.

Related recurring shapes seen in the same audit:
- Quoted metrics in a verdict doc traced to a **gitignored** log file, while a
  *different* log with *different* numbers was the one actually committed.
  Check that the numbers in the prose match the committed artifact, not just
  that some artifact exists.
- Claims of the form "N/N checks passed" (unit tables, synthetic replays) with
  no committed harness or output. Phase 0 declared "evidence artifacts stand in
  for tests" — so a missing artifact is a missing test.

**How to apply:** for every evidence claim, run `git ls-files <path>` and
`git check-ignore -v <path>`. Grep the verdict's exact numbers against the
committed file's contents. Treat working-tree-only evidence as FAIL on
"committed", even when the content is correct.

**Phase 4 recurrence (2026-08-21), in the orchestrator-salvaged `src/perf/` package:**

- `src/perf/perf.test.ts` references `EVIDENCE.md` **twice** (lines 74 and ~391) as the place the
  FULL-run numbers and the DoD verdict were written. **No such file exists, anywhere, ever** —
  `git ls-files | grep -i evidence` returns only `docs/evidence/ui-states/`, `fixtures/SCRUB-EVIDENCE.md`
  and `fixtures/phase0-evidence/`. The DoD line it was meant to satisfy is "memory bounded (heap
  evidence committed)".
- The justification for widening a threshold (1200 -> 2500 ms) rests on two runs whose medians
  (555.3 ms) and slowest sample (727.1 ms) exist **only as prose in `budgets.ts`**. The harness has
  `AGENT_DECK_PERF_RECORD=<path>` which emits exactly that record as JSON, and nobody used it. A
  measurement that a tool could have committed and did not is unverifiable by design.

**How to apply, added:** grep every doc-comment reference to a sibling file and confirm the file
exists. "Recorded in X" where X is absent is the same failure as "committed" where nothing is
tracked.

name: pattern-counts-measured-before-own-commit
description: Git-derived counts (blobs, commits) written into the very commit that changes them — 1017/325/176 were all off by exactly the session's own commit
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

**Every git-derived number in a handover — blob counts, commit counts, ahead-counts — must be
re-derived at the commit the document claims to describe. Ask "does this count include the commit
this document is in?" It usually does not.**

**Why:** `release-prep-0.5.0`'s handover (2026-08-30) stated its gate table was "Measured on the
tree at public `b96d802`" and gave three numbers that were all taken at the parent `d81cfe6`:

| claim | at `d81cfe6` | at `b96d802` |
|---|---:|---:|
| sweep history blobs | **1017** | 1030 |
| public commits (`--all`) | **325** | 326 |
| lab commits (`--all`) | **176** (at `2d11310`) | 177 |

The blob gap is exactly the 13 blobs the commit adds (4 added + 9 modified files). Reproduce with:

```
git rev-list --all --objects | cut -d' ' -f1 | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype)' | sort | uniq -c
# and for the parent state, feed explicit refs to `git rev-list --objects --stdin`
```

**The expensive part is that a wrong number got a conclusion built on it.** A deviation argued the
fresh clone "is the better measurement anyway — it swept **1030**, more than the local run's
**1017**". The local run sweeps 1030 too; the difference was the commit, not clone-vs-local. A
stale number is cheap, but reasoning *from the delta between two differently-dated measurements* is
a false finding.

**The irony to expect:** the same document correctly diagnosed this exact class for someone else's
number (`CLAUDE.md`'s 2140 suite total, six short because the audit added six tests in the session
that wrote the block) and committed it three times itself. Catching the class looking backwards does
not stop an author committing it looking forwards — so check the author's own numbers hardest.

**2026-08-31, `release-readme-trim`: the class recurred INSIDE its own correction.** A paragraph
whose whole subject was "a number in this block was written before the block was finished" stated
`git diff --numstat` on `docs/evidence/phase-9/VERIFY.md` as **49 insertions / 15 deletions**.
Measured at audit time: **62 / 15**. The gap is exactly 13 = the 9-line parenthetical making the
claim + a 4-line note the same session added lower in the file. The 15-deletion half and its
"1 mine / 14 the user's" split were both correct. **The insertion half of a numstat is the half
that counts your own still-unwritten prose** — re-run `git diff --numstat` as the LAST edit, after
the paragraph quoting it exists.

Related: [[pattern_report_json_numbers]], [[pattern_default_limit_becomes_all]],
[[pattern_prose_line_references_drift]].

Supersedes the v0.6.0 PLAN in full (archived in Phase 0 under `docs/` as the next free `PLAN-vN.md`;
re-measure with `ls docs/PLAN-v*.md`). Spec: `agent-deck-spec.md` + **Amendment 2026-09-04 —
Layer 1** (lands as DoD 0.1, inserted before the Version-posture section, before any code).

**Baseline (re-measure, do not read):** `vsce show nvitlam.agent-deck` reports `0.6.0`; `main` carries
the `v0.6.0` tag; `package.json` `displayName` is "Agent Deck — Watch Your Agents Work."; engines
present: `src/parser` (CC), `src/opencode`, `src/codex`. If any of these is false, stop at the gate.

**What this release is:** deterministic facts from the session model of all three engines, a local
append-only history of those facts, a Stats view mode, an activity-bar entry with a command menu, the
deck opening in the left editor group, and an extension API exposing the facts. It says
nothing about why and recommends nothing. Interpretation is Layer 2, a separate closed repo
(`agent-deck-insights`), not designed until this ships.

---

## Grounding Contract (build-time law — applies to every phase)

G1, G5, G8, G9 carried forward verbatim from the v0.6.0 PLAN (G1 already names `~/.claude`, the
OpenCode data/config directories and `~/.codex`/`$CODEX_HOME`). Changed or added:

- **G2 — Source separation, extended.** The stats deriver is a third consumer downstream of every
  engine's grafter. It never feeds liveness or content. A deriver failure increments `statsErrors` on
  the diagnostics channel and is skipped; the deck renders identically with the deriver present,
  absent, or throwing.
- **G3 — Refuse, don't guess, extended.** Stats derive only for sessions with `schemaOk: true` and an
  empty `parked`. Everything else is `excluded:<code>`, empty tables, absent from every aggregate.
- **G4 — Redaction, extended.** `StatsRecord` string fields are an allow-list. A corpus test asserts,
  against literal captured bytes from all three corpora, that no thinking/reasoning, payload, or
  message text appears in any record or store file.
- **G6 — Fixtures are law, extended.** One committed golden `StatsRecord` per committed session
  fixture, all engines, regenerated only by script.
- **G7 — Live-only, in-memory, AMENDED.** No persistence under any engine's directory; no replay.
  Derived stats MAY persist under `globalStorageUri`, append-only, retention-bounded, user-clearable,
  disableable. Never read back into `SessionState`.
- **G10 — Facts only (new).** No interpretive language in `src/stats/**`, `webview/stats/**`, or the
  `0.7.0` CHANGELOG block. The forbidden-word script is a lint gate from the moment the UI exists.

**Process law:** unchanged. Implementer worktrees commit before DONE; orchestrator writes glue only.
Budget law: write all code, run the suite once, fix, run again. Live sessions buy engine evidence only;
renderer evidence comes from R6 wire replay. **Reserved to the user:** everything on CLAUDE.md's
reserved list — in particular `vsce publish`, any move of `main`, amending G-letters (this plan
records the user's decision; CC does not re-decide it), and the `OWN-EYES.md` signature.

**Re-measurement commands (every phase, before the open-question gate):**
`git log --oneline -5` · `git status --short` · `node scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs` ·
`npx vitest run --reporter=dot 2>&1 | tail -3` · `ls fixtures/ | grep -E '^(cc|opencode|codex)-'`.

# VERDICT — Phase 0, fact derivability spike (binary gate)

**THE RELEASE IS NOT KILLED. Every floor fact is DERIVABLE on the Claude Code corpus.**

DoD 0.5 sets the floor at **F1, F3, F5, F11 on the CC corpus** and says that if any floor fact is
`DROPPED` the release is killed and this line says so. None is. Measured over 9 CC sessions:

| floor fact | CC verdict | sessions with the input present | sessions where it fired |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F1** per-file counts | **DERIVABLE** | 5 of 9 | 5 |
| **F3** identical-call loop | **DERIVABLE** | 8 of 9 | 1 |
| **F5** burn | **DERIVABLE** | 9 of 9 | 9 |
| **F11** attribution coverage | **DERIVABLE** | 9 of 9 | 9 |

**Nothing is `DROPPED`.** `DROPPED` means a fact needs the *text* of a message or payload, which
Layer 1 forbids. No fact reached that state: every one is either derivable on an engine or
`UNAVAILABLE` on it because the engine states no such field.

---

## Method, and what would make it wrong

`spike/stats/derive-facts.mjs`, `node:` builtins only, importing nothing from `src/`. That
independence is the point: a fact derived by the engine under test is not evidence that the fact is
derivable. `spike/stats/toolclass-census.mjs` supplies the tool classes and file-argument keys and
is the same shape.

**Structure only.** Every value read is a named field or a key of a structured input object. No
regex touches message or payload text. That constraint decides one outcome rather than merely
constraining style, and it is recorded under F2/F4 below.

**Scope.** 23 sessions across 11 corpora — 9 CC, 9 OpenCode, 5 Codex. The three anchors are
re-measured at run time from the fingerprint modules (`cc-2.1.246`, `opencode-1.18.22`,
`codex-0.151.0-alpha.7.2`), never written down: a corpus is an anchor because a fingerprint pins it.

**12 corpora were skipped and the run says so by name** (rule 18): `golden`, `hook-events`, `hooks`,
`phase0-evidence`, `synthetic-codex-structure`, `synthetic-graft`, `synthetic-hook-fuzz`,
`synthetic-layout`, `synthetic-lines`, `synthetic-path-matrix`, `synthetic-perf`,
`synthetic-structure-2.1.246`. They are refusal and mutation fixtures, not session recordings.

**A first draft got that wrong and the number is why it was caught.** It classified any directory
holding a `.jsonl` whose first line contains `"payload"` as a Codex corpus, which swept in
`synthetic-codex-structure` — 37 hand-made single-line mutation fixtures, each reporting as a
"session" with no usage, making every Codex column read `5/42` instead of `5/5`. Corpus
discovery is now structural in both directions: an `opencode.db` anywhere beneath the corpus (not
at its root — `opencode-1.18.25` keeps its store in `moved-project/` and a root-only test silently
skipped it), a rollout under a `sessions/` directory (14 of 14 real files, 0 of 37 synthetic), or a
`projects/` directory.

---

## DoD 0.4 — the fact × engine table

`present` = the structure the fact needs exists in that session. `fired` = it produced at least one
row. **Both are reported because they answer different questions**: a fact can be perfectly
derivable and legitimately fire zero times, because the session contained no loop and no churn.
Zero firings is not evidence of a missing field, and a single flag cannot say which.

| fact | cc | opencode | codex |
|---|---|---|---|
| **F1** per-file read/edit/write/error + first/last ordinal | DERIVABLE 5/5 of 9 | DERIVABLE 7/7 of 9 | **UNAVAILABLE:codex** |
| **F2** per-tool calls, errors, duration | DERIVABLE 8/8 of 9 | DERIVABLE 7/7 of 9 | DERIVABLE 5/5 of 5 *(errors unavailable)* |
| **F3** identical-call loop | DERIVABLE 8/1 of 9 | DERIVABLE 7/1 of 9 | DERIVABLE 5/1 of 5 |
| **F4** churn chain | DERIVABLE 3/2 of 9 | DERIVABLE 3/0 of 9 | **UNAVAILABLE:codex** |
| **F5** burn per agent and tree | DERIVABLE 9/9 of 9 | DERIVABLE 8/8 of 9 | DERIVABLE 5/5 of 5 |
| **F6** cache ratio | DERIVABLE 9/9 of 9 | DERIVABLE 8/8 of 9 | DERIVABLE 5/5 of 5 |
| **F7** context churn | DERIVABLE 8/5 of 9 | DERIVABLE 5/0 of 9 | DERIVABLE 5/0 of 5 |
| **F8** subagents, silent subagents | DERIVABLE 9/6 of 9 | DERIVABLE 9/2 of 9 | DERIVABLE 5/4 of 5 |
| **F9** cost | **UNAVAILABLE** | **UNAVAILABLE** | **UNAVAILABLE** |
| **F10** context fill | **UNAVAILABLE:cc** | **UNAVAILABLE:opencode** | DERIVABLE 5/5 of 5 |
| **F11** attribution coverage | DERIVABLE 9/9 of 9 | DERIVABLE 9/9 of 9 | DERIVABLE 5/5 of 5 |

### The four `UNAVAILABLE` findings, with their causes

**F9 — cost is unavailable on ALL THREE engines, and this is the finding most likely to surprise.**

## DoD 0.6 — the two constants

### `SPIKE_TOKENS = 4000`

**The locked scope was degenerate and the constant is therefore measured on a wider one, stated
here rather than applied silently.** The rule is "the value at which ≤ 5 % of real turns across the
anchor corpora qualify, rounded to the nearest thousand".

| scope | quantity | n | non-zero | p50 | p90 | p95 | max |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| anchors | turn-over-turn delta | 174 | **1** | 0 | 0 | **0** | 70 |
| anchors | per-turn level | 214 | 9 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 41,388 |
| captured | turn-over-turn delta | 709 | 228 | 0 | 1,775 | **3,319** | 710,119 |
| captured | per-turn level | 770 | 490 | 687 | 4,008 | 8,768 | 710,550 |

The anchors' 95th-percentile delta is **0**, with exactly one non-zero delta in 174. Every positive
threshold satisfies "≤ 5 % qualify", so the rule selects nothing and any constant read off it is a
floored guess wearing a measurement's clothes. The anchors are **provenance** anchors, not
representative sessions — `cc-2.1.246` is a 16-line scripted mirror pair. The constant is therefore
taken over every **captured** session corpus (synthetic excluded, G6).

**And the rounding rule had to be inverted.** Rounding p95 = 3,319 to the *nearest* thousand gives
3,000, which admits **5.6 %** — above the rule's own ceiling. The ≤ 5 % property is the rule and
rounding is presentation, so the constant is the smallest whole thousand that actually satisfies it:
**4,000, admitting 29 of 709 turns = 4.1 %.**

Both candidate quantities are tabulated because spec §D names the *delta* and a reader who assumed
the *level* would derive a different constant (8,768 → 9,000). The delta is what is used.

### `LOOP_MIN = 3`

The spec default, confirmed rather than moved. Repeat counts of one `toolName + inputHash` within
one agent:

| scope | distinct call signatures | ≥2 | ≥3 | ≥4 | ≥5 | ≥6 | ≥8 | ≥10 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| anchors | 281 | 4 | 2 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| captured | 889 | 5 | 3 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 0 |

At 3 it selects **3 loops in 889 signatures**; at 2 it selects 5. The distribution is long-tailed and
sparse, so the threshold is not sensitive between 3 and 4 — 3 is kept because the spec names it and
nothing measured argues against it. The three loops it selects are real and one per engine:
`Bash × 5` (cc-2.1.237), `task × 9` (opencode-1.18.22), `wait_agent × 4` (codex).

**`inputHash` is SHA-256 over canonical JSON** — keys sorted at every depth, arrays left in order
because order is meaning there.

content.content:
# `cc-2.1.260` — the COMPACTION corpus

Captured 2026-09-05 for v0.7.0 Phase 0, DoD 0.3b. Real Claude Code session, captured raw and then
redacted; G6 applies to it exactly as it applies to every other corpus here.

**Why it exists.** No committed corpus held a structural compaction entry, so fact **F12**
(compaction events: count, ordinal, turns since session start, prompt tokens either side) rested on
nothing. This session holds **two** compactions of **different triggers**, which is what makes it
able to answer the question rather than merely exhibit one.

**It also closes two gaps nobody harvested it for**, and both are worth more than they cost:

- **The only real `Edit` calls in any committed corpus.** Before this, `Edit` appeared **only** in
  `fixtures/synthetic-dropped-actions/` (32 calls, hand-made). Fact **F4** — the churn chain — is
  defined on `Edit/Write`, so its entire evidence base was synthetic. This corpus carries **18 real
  `Edit` calls** beside 32 `Write` and 39 `Read`.
- **A real mid-file CC version change.** The session's lines carry **two** versions (below). Every
  earlier mid-file-drift case in this repository is synthetic. This one is real and it is
  *in-window*, so it is a positive control for the version posture: it must be **accepted**.

## Provenance

| | |
|---|---|
| session | `75ef0bbf-2493-4c77-8af7-3a56fb2ce36e` |
| captured | 2026-09-05, from this machine's live `~/.claude/projects/` |
| lines | 2,028 parsed, **0 malformed** |
| versions on the lines | `2.1.258` ×1,225 and `2.1.260` ×201 |
| subagents | 3, each with its `.meta.json` sidecar |
| `tool-results/` | 1 offloaded payload |
| tool calls | `Bash` 218 · `Read` 39 · `Write` 32 · `Edit` 18 · `Skill` 3 · `Agent` 3 · `ToolSearch` 2 · `TaskStop` 1 |

**The directory is named `cc-2.1.260`, and the majority of its lines say `2.1.258`.** That is
deliberate and it is the honest name: **both compaction entries are written by `2.1.260`**, and the
compaction entries are the reason the corpus exists. Naming it for the majority version would name
it for the half that proves nothing. The version is read from the transcript's own `version` field,
never from the binary on `PATH` — the recorded rule, and this session is its own illustration, since
one binary wrote lines under two version strings.

## The two compaction entries

The structural entry is `type: "system"` carrying a `compactMetadata` object. Each is immediately
followed by a `type: "user"` entry with `isCompactSummary: true` — the summary CC injects in place
of what it dropped.

| line | type | `trigger` | `preTokens` | `postTokens` | `cumulativeDroppedTokens` |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| **1933** | `system` | **`auto`** | 967,149 | 20,346 | 946,803 |
| 1934 | `user` | — (`isCompactSummary: true`) | | | |
| **2006** | `system` | **`manual`** (a `/compact`) | 276,178 | 24,938 | 1,198,043 |
| 2007 | `user` | — (`isCompactSummary: true`) | | | |

**Do their shapes match? YES — the key sets are identical**, measured rather than eyeballed. Both
`compactMetadata` objects carry exactly:

`cumulativeDroppedTokens`, `durationMs`, `postTokens`, `preCompactDiscoveredTools`, `preTokens`,
`preservedMessages`, `preservedSegment`, `trigger`

They differ only in **key order** within the object, which JSON does not carry meaning in, and in
their values. So per the locked Phase 0 answer: **a manual `/compact` is a valid F12 fixture
source** — one reader handles both, and `trigger` is what separates them, so F12 can record
`source: 'auto' | 'manual'` from the entry itself with nothing inferred.

**`preTokens` and `postTokens` are stated by the entry.** F12 wanted "prompt tokens on the turn
before and after **where the entries state them**"; here they are stated outright, so that half of
F12 needs no turn-walking at all.

## What was done to the bytes

Two redactors, in this order. Both are the existing route; neither is new for this corpus.

1. **`lab/tools/redact-paths.mjs`** (identity-token driven, 45 tokens, the private set) —
   `files=8 changed=4 renamed=0 exempt=0 **skipped=0**`, 905 replacements across ten token classes.
2. **`scripts/redact-paths.mjs`** (path shapes → `<HOME>`/`<USER>`/`<HOST>`) — `files=8 skipped=0
   changed=4`, 1,175 hits.

Before either, the repository path and the project slug were rewritten to the same scrubbed form
every other committed CC corpus already carries — slug `c--Users-dev-projects-agent-deck`, `cwd`
`C:\Users\dev\projects\agent-deck` — in all four spellings that occur (JSON-escaped, Windows,
forward-slash, MSYS). 2,671 replacements.

**The slug needs its own step because the redactor deliberately will not touch it**: the slug uses
`-` as its separator so no absolute-path pattern matches it, and it is a **join key**
(`projectSlug`; `src/opencode/slug.ts` pins the two engines' agreement on it). It is also identity
token #1, and the identity class has **no allow rule** — a hit fails the gate outright. Leaving it
alone was therefore not an option, and rewriting it by hand was.

**`node scripts/privacy-sweep.mjs --untracked` → `VERDICT PASS identity=0 secrets=0 foreign=0`.**
It read `FAIL identity=527` before the identity redactor ran, on the untracked working tree, which
is the order that matters: nothing was committed until it read zero.

**What redaction did NOT move**, verified after the fact: line count, parse result (2,028 / 0
malformed), both version strings and their counts, every tool-call name and count, all three
sidecars, the offloaded payload, and both `compactMetadata` objects including every token figure in

## E. Model-boundary additions

All computed at each engine's parse boundary, **before truncation**, all redaction-safe:

- `ToolNode.filePath?: string` — the structured file argument of file-class tools. The set of file-class
  tool names and their argument keys is a **census table** derived from the corpus in Phase 0
  (`src/stats/toolclass.ts`, generated, per engine). Unknown tools → class `other`, no `filePath`.
- `ToolNode.inputHash: string` — SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the full structured tool input,
  computed before `previewBytes` truncation. A hash is not content and survives G4.
- `ToolNode.ordinal: number` — explicit position within the agent, so F4 needs no tree walk.
- `AgentNode.model?: string` — the model id as written by the engine, verbatim, for F9(b).
- `AgentNode.compactions?: CompactionEvent[]` — `{ ordinal, promptBefore?, promptAfter? }` from the
  engine's structural compaction entry; optional per engine (Phase 0).
- `AgentNode.usageSeries?: UsageTurn[]` — ordered `{ ordinal, input, cacheCreation, cacheRead,
  output }` per distinct message id, the same de-dup the existing `burn` arithmetic uses; optional
  because an engine may not supply it. Where present, its sum **equals** `burn` (tested).

Per engine: CC — all four from `tool_use` blocks and `usage`. Codex — from rollout tool items;
`usageSeries` per Phase 0 measurement. OpenCode — `filePath`/`inputHash` from part rows;
`usageSeries` only if `step-finish` rows carry the split (Phase 0), else `unavailable`.

**Golden blast radius (enumerated in Phase 0, matched exactly in Phase 1):** `fixtures/golden/session/`,

**B3 — The CC engine STAMPS `engine: 'cc'`. Absence stops being the CC signal.**

Today only `src/opencode/` writes the field, and `src/model/events.ts` documents absence as reading

wire names its engine. Absence remains valid at the type level — the field stays optional, because
making it required would break every earlier construction of the interface, which is the whole
reason it was added optional three times over.

**Blast radius, measured before the decision:** `fixtures/golden/session/` (two files, regenerated
by `src/model/session.test.ts`) and `webview/wire/` (**one** file — corrected below). `fixtures/golden/graft/` does **not** change — the CC grafter produces a
`GraftSnapshot`, not a `SessionState`. `webview/goldens/layout/` does not change: layout is geometry
and geometry does not read the tag.

**`webview/wire/` holds two files and only ONE of them moves.** This block originally said both
were "regenerated by `scripts/record-wire.mjs`", which the phase verifier disproved:
`webview/wire/synthetic-stress.json` records `"producedBy": "webview/stress.test.ts"` and is not
produced by `record-wire.mjs` at all. It is built by hand and never drives `SessionModel`, so B3's
stamping cannot reach it — `webview/wire.test.ts` carries an assertion whose whole job is to leave
it alone. Only `cc-2.1.234-session-arc.json` is recorded through the real host model, and only it
gained the tag. The line is corrected here because it was offered as a *measurement*, and a
measurement that is wrong on one of its two terms is worth more as a correction than as a quiet
edit.

**This is why the wire corpus is regenerated in a LATER WAVE than the model change**, and the
sequencing is part of the decision rather than an implementation detail. `record-wire.mjs` records
traffic by driving the **real** `SessionModel`. Regenerating the corpus before the stamping lands

in the full suite. That is `CLAUDE.md`'s "a merge falsified a test both halves passed", and this
